paper_metadata.title: Applying the Quantum Grover Algorithm to Improve the Efﬁciency of Growth Models

experiments.description: Classical dynamic control optimization experiment presented as the paper's main numerical study; despite the paper's quantum framing, the reported implementation uses numerical optimization of nonlinear differential equations with SLSQP and does not provide an actual executed quantum circuit.

algorithm.variant: dynamic control optimization with numerical minimization; quantum methods discussed conceptually (VQE, Grover, QAOA) but not experimentally executed

problem_formulation.objective_function: J = integral_0^T c(x(t), u(t)) dt + phi(x(T)); in the implemented pseudocode J = integral of squares of (x^2 + u^2) plus x_T^2
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: control bounds u in [-1, 1]; state/action dynamics enforced by differential equation integration

problem_instance.description: Nonlinear time-varying control system with dynamics dx/dt = sin(x(t)) + u(t), and a second illustrative linear system dx/dt = -a x(t) + b u(t)

dataset_specification.description: No dataset; synthetic control problem with continuous-time dynamics

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Numerical integration of the differential equation over [0, T] using the provided system_dynamics procedure; control vector clipped to bounds before optimization
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Single optimization run reported with resulting control vector and objective value

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: clip control values to bounds; discretize control via index mapping over time interval
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: extract final state x_T and compute integral cost plus terminal cost

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper discusses quantum methods conceptually (VQE, Grover, QAOA) but the reported numerical experiment is a classical numerical optimization of a nonlinear differential equation using SLSQP; no executed quantum circuit or quantum-vs-classical benchmark is provided.

experiments.description: Grover-algorithm-based theoretical optimization for economic growth models, specifically Solow and Cobb-Douglas parameter search and steady-state stability analysis; the paper provides derivations but no executed quantum hardware experiment.

algorithm.variant: Grover search for optimal parameters in economic growth models

problem_formulation.encoding_details: binary function over n-bit input register; search for x0 such that f(x0)=1
problem_formulation.objective_function: Find parameters maximizing economic model efficiency / identify optimal x0 in an unstructured search formulation; Solow steady state defined by s f(k*) = (n + delta) k* and Cobb-Douglas steady state by s A (K*)^alpha L^(1-alpha) = delta K*
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: oracle-based marked-state search; no explicit penalty formulation reported

problem_instance.description: Parameter optimization and steady-state stability analysis for the Solow growth model and the Cobb-Douglas production model

dataset_specification.description: Analytical economic models; no empirical dataset

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Model equations are derived symbolically; no data preprocessing reported
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: The paper provides theoretical complexity comparison and qualitative discussion; no numerical benchmark or repeated-run evaluation reported
